Research record / Preprint

VARZIN V2 — Recoverable but Not Composable: Representation Recovery and Systematic Composition in a Frozen Language Model

Frozen Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct strongly encodes the tested synthetic morphological-position variable in a linearly decodable form across held-out contexts, but the preregistered downstream composition test produced 0/58 passes. This is evidence for a separation in this experiment, not a universal theorem that decodability never implies composability.

V1.02026-09-09ZenodoPreprint
Evidence status

Strong representation-recovery result paired with a clean preregistered negative composition result. Publication status: Preprint / results-locked research report; not treated as peer-reviewed validation.

01 / question

Research question and current reading.

Research question

Does strong recovery of a structural variable from a frozen model imply that the model can use that representation as a substrate for systematic compositional generalization?

Frozen Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct strongly encodes the tested synthetic morphological-position variable in a linearly decodable form across held-out contexts, but the preregistered downstream composition test produced 0/58 passes. This is evidence for a separation in this experiment, not a universal theorem that decodability never implies composability.

02 / methods

What was actually tested.

  • Phase 0: construct, leakage-audit, and cryptographically freeze a 10,800-record synthetic dataset with 12 positions and 30 contexts.
  • Phase 1: evaluate surface-span, whole-sentence, and last-token representations across all 29 hidden-state indices without holdout-driven best-layer selection.
  • Phase 2: test k = (i + j) mod 12 on 144 ordered pairs (120 train, 24 fixed holdout), 30 realizations per pair, and 10 preregistered seeds.
  • Compare TRUE against SHUFFLED, WRONG_OP, and RANDOM conditions; require both paired exact sign-flip p < 0.01 and ≥0.15 balanced-accuracy margin against every control.
03 / results

Strongest supported findings.

  • Phase 1 surface-span mean BA across 29 indices = 0.9666; median = 1.000; 25/29 indices reach BA = 1.000, while embedding index 0 is at chance (0.0833).
  • Phase 2 verdict: PASS 0/58, AMBIGUOUS 0/58, FAIL 58/58.
  • Closest positive TRUE-vs-control effect = +0.082 BA (MLP, layer 5 vs RANDOM), exact sign-flip p = 0.1719—well below the preregistered +0.15 / p<0.01 thresholds.
  • The failure is not explained by constant-output collapse: most evaluated rows use the full 12-class output space.
04 / scale & benchmark lineage

How this experiment relates to Core-30 and later scaled benchmarks.

VARZIN V2 frozen dataset

10,800 records

A distinct synthetic morphological-position dataset with 12 structural positions, 30 contexts, 24 training contexts, 6 held-out contexts, and 30 instances per position/context configuration.

Representation evaluation

29 hidden-state indices

Surface-span mean reached mean balanced accuracy 0.9666; 25/29 indices reached 1.000 under held-out-context evaluation.

Composition evaluation

144 ordered pairs / 58 layer-composer combinations

120 training pairs and 24 fixed held-out pairs; final preregistered verdict 0/58 PASS, 58/58 FAIL.

Scale boundary: Core-30 remains a canonical reference subset. Larger generated corpora and later benchmark datasets are distinct experimental artifacts and should not be silently relabeled as a single enlarged canonical lexicon.

05 / falsification

Negative findings are part of the result.

  • Strong linear decodability did not translate into detected systematic generalization of the TRUE composition rule on unseen ordered pairs.
  • The post-hoc Latin-square pattern is explicitly exploratory/hypothesis-generating, not confirmatory.
  • The study does not show that Qwen lacks all algebraic structure or that language models generally cannot compose.
06 / limits

What this record does not establish.

  • The result is tied to the frozen Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct protocol, synthetic structure, fixed composers, and stated decision rule.
  • Historical v1.4 identity remains unresolved; the frozen V2 artifact is an independently generated/audited artifact, not claimed byte-identical to that historical selection.
  • Generalization to other models, natural language, operations, and readout architectures remains open.

Boundary: a Zenodo deposit is a citable public record; it does not by itself imply peer review, independent validation, causal inference, or generalization beyond the documented experiment.

10 / version provenance

Keep this deposit distinct from later interpretation.

The study separates representation recovery from composition and records that successful recovery alone is insufficient evidence for systematic generalization. This is a narrower and more defensible conclusion than treating probe success as proof of compositional competence.

Version V1.0 is the current public Zenodo record listed by VARZIN for the integrated Phase 0–2 report. Any later remediation or follow-up experiment should be cited separately from this fixed deposit.
